extracted.intended_audience: general Canadian readers and comedy/festival audiences
extracted.subtask_description: A news announcement describing the lineup, programming and organizational goals for the Montreal Just For Laughs summer festival (JFL), including managerial changes after bankruptcy and programming highlights. Intended to inform potential attendees and the comedy community about the festival's return and format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comedy-first approach
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'comedy first' approach — a revitalized focus on prioritizing comedy in festival decisions (phrasing: "revitalized focus he called a 'comedy first' approach").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Festival leadership frames programming and operational choices around a stated priority for comedy and comedic integrity. Parent-Bédard: 'I have my hands on the wheel... decisions about love for comedy, about passion.' The approach is presented as a guiding principle rather than a technical rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mix of new faces and well-known artists
rubrics_metrics.description: Offer audiences a mix of new faces and well-known artists (phrasing: 'this year's edition will offer audiences a mix of new faces and well-known artists').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programming should balance emerging talent and established acts to rebuild the festival's legacy and appeal broadly. Presented as part of the festival's strategy to rejuvenate reputation after financial troubles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comedians and fans having fun (primary success metric)
rubrics_metrics.description: The most important thing is 'comedians having fun, fans having fun' — enjoyment as a central measure of success.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leadership explicitly states performer and audience enjoyment as a core evaluative criterion for the festival's success, prioritizing atmosphere and performer experience alongside commercial or prestige goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stable festival / financial recovery
rubrics_metrics.description: Put in place 'a great festival, a stable festival' — emphasis on organizational and financial stability after bankruptcy and asset sale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stability is framed as essential: the article references JFL's 2024 bankruptcy, acquisition by ComediHa!, and the need to rebuild financially and institutionally. Programming and scale choices (e.g., scaled-down editions previously) are tied to stabilizing the organization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Headline booking of high-profile comedians
rubrics_metrics.description: Booking prominent headliners (examples listed: Tom Segura, Russell Peters, Russell Howard, Mae Martin, Kumail Nanjiani, Fortune Feimster, Michelle Buteau, Adam Ray) to anchor the festival.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High-profile names are used as indicators of the festival's stature and to attract audiences and media; presence of big names signals a return toward 'industry powerhouse' status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Programming variety across formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a range of formats: solo standup shows, gala series, comedy club series, concerts, and outdoor shows (phrasing: 'in addition to solo standup shows... two free outdoor comedy shows and the return of the festival's comedy club series').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Diverse show formats are presented as important to appeal to varied audiences, support different kinds of performers, and restore the festival's comprehensive offering.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revival of gala series and broadcast tapings
rubrics_metrics.description: Revive gala series featuring breakout acts with industry veterans and tape shows to air on broadcasters (phrasing: 'JFL is also reviving its gala series... taped in front of a live audience, to air on CBC').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gala and broadcast partnerships (CBC, Roast Battle Canada taping) serve as both programming highlights and distribution/marketing mechanisms that amplify festival reach and prestige.

rubrics_metrics.name: Free outdoor shows / accessibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Schedule free outdoor comedy shows (phrasing: 'plans this summer include two free outdoor comedy shows').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Free events are highlighted as a tactic to increase accessibility, community engagement, and public visibility of the festival beyond ticketed venues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for diverse and international talent
rubrics_metrics.description: Showcase diverse and international performers (examples: Toronto's Mae Martin, Pakistani-American Kumail Nanjiani, Cameroon-born Steve Biko, U.S. comics listed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lineup diversity is implied as a desirable characteristic—representing local Canadian artists alongside international comedians to reflect inclusivity and broad appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Positive community and industry impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Position the festival as 'good news for the community... good news for the [comedy] industry' — cultural and economic benefits to Montreal and the comedy ecosystem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Festival success is framed not only in artistic terms but as delivering community value and supporting the wider comedy industry; statements emphasize local pride and industry revival as outcomes.
